fieldNotes.facilityId: Constellation Gonzales Winery confirmed at 800 S Alta St, Gonzales CA. The large warehouse + tank farm + crush-pad campus NE of the road is the winery. The SW industrial building with a heavy trailer yard is a SEPARATE company - Braga Fresh produce (500 S Alta St) - confirmed by a 'braga ... LINE TRUCK ENTRANCE' sign in Street View; it was excluded from this audit.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Winery main entrance is a divided in/out road off the public road at the SE of the campus, with a small admin/office structure beside it. No barrier arm or sliding/swing gate is visible across the truck lane in satellite imagery; Street View does not cover the private drive. Treated as an open/uncontrolled industrial entrance - marked false but low confidence.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Small structure near the entrance road appears to be an administrative/reception office, not a dedicated 1-3-vehicle guard booth set beside a gated lane. No guard shack identified.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: No truck gate identified, so remoteGs is false.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: The entrance road is physically divided into separate inbound and outbound lanes with painted ENTER/EXIT pavement markings.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide divided entrance road and large paved aprons/circulation areas leave ample room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long approach: the entrance road runs several hundred feet from the public road, past the south admin buildings and around a landscaped oval, before reaching the production area - easily holds a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Winery production campus, not a freight DC. No long bank of freight dock doors visible. Estimate ~6-12 service/loading doors across the warehouse south face and crush-pad service area. Low confidence from overhead imagery.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A modest number of trailers (roughly 6-10) seen parked along internal roads and the crush-pad area; not a large dedicated marked drop lot. Banded 0-10, low confidence.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Grape intake / crush pad (receiving) is physically distinct from the finished-goods warehouse and tank-farm loading area - effectively separate receiving and shipping zones.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved circulation/holding areas inside the property between the entrance and the production buildings provide internal staging.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus with multiple distinct large buildings: the main warehouse, the open-air tank farm, a crush/processing structure, and a south administrative/processing building cluster.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh platform clearly identified in the truck path; marked false with low confidence (a harvest grape scale may exist but is not confirmed in imagery).
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the US-101 corridor on the east side of the property, but no rail spur enters the winery property.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge of the small town of Gonzales, Monterey County - surrounded by farmland and vineyards, well outside any dense metro fabric.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Rural, but immediately adjacent to the town of Gonzales and US-101 with normal cellular coverage; connectivityIssue false.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Approximately 8 trailers visible in captured imagery on the winery property (excluding the Braga Fresh yard); honest estimate.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Ample paved space could hold ~20 trailers, but the site is not laid out as a dedicated drop yard; estimate.

citations.claim: The Wine Group names Gonzales as one of its NEW winemaking sites ('its other new winemaking site is in Gonzales, about five miles north of its plant in Soledad, Monterey County') acquired from Constellation
TWG completed acquisition of Constellation production sites including a Monterey County, CA site (plus Lodi and SIMI Healdsburg), ~6,600 vineyard acres and ~500 employees
Constellation divested mainstream wine brands (Woodbridge, Meiomi, Robert Mondavi Private Selection, Cook's, SIMI, J. Roget) plus associated facilities and vineyards to The Wine Group

verification.rationale: DIVESTED: this Monterey County bulk-wine production winery transferred to The Wine Group when the deal closed 2025-06-02; TWG's own July 2025 newsroom explicitly names Gonzales as a new acquired site. No longer Constellation-operated. Roster's 'retained after sale' assumption was wrong.
